title: vlad chituc
text:
about
I’m a postdoctoral researcher at Stanford University. I spent seven years as a Writing Consultant at Yale’s Graduate Writing Lab, where I worked with hundreds of students across every discipline — on dissertations, journal articles, fellowship applications, and personal statements.
I ran yearly workshops for NSF Graduate Research Fellowship applications and personal statement workshops for Yale Psychology’s graduate admissions program. Before Yale, I was published in The New York Times, The New Republic, and The Daily Beast.
I also spent a year mentoring advanced high school students through a structured research program — guiding them from reading scientific papers through writing their own college-level research reports.
What I’m good at: understanding what you’re trying to say and helping you say it more clearly, in your own voice. I won’t rewrite your essay for you. I’ll help you figure out what makes your story compelling and how to tell it well.

title: vlad chituc
text:
frequently asked questions


Will you write my essay for me?
No. Your essay needs to sound like you, and admissions officers are very good at spotting essays that don’t. I’ll give you detailed feedback on what’s working, what isn’t, and how to make it better — but you do the writing. That’s also what makes the essay actually good.


What kinds of essays do you review?
Common App personal statements, Coalition essays, supplemental essays (Why This School, community, activity, etc.), UC PIQs, scholarship essays, and anything else that’s part of a college application.


When should I start?
The earlier the better. Most students benefit from starting over the summer before senior year. The Common App opens August 1, and early decision deadlines are typically November 1. That said, I work with students at every stage — if you have a draft due next week, I can help with that too.

title: consulting
text:
measurement & survey design
If your work involves asking people to rate things on a scale — customer satisfaction, political attitudes, content moderation, RLHF preference ratings — I can help you think about what those numbers actually mean and how to interpret them correctly. This is what my research is about, and it turns out the standard practices are worse than most people realize.
I can help you design better surveys, audit your existing ones, and analyze your data so you can get a fuller picture. I’m also available for talks and workshops for research teams.

title: consulting
text:
writing
I’ve written for The New York Times, The New Republic, and The Daily Beast, and I’ve spent a lot of time helping other people express themselves clearly in writing. I worked for seven years as a Writing Consultant at Yale’s Graduate Writing Lab, where I worked with students across all disciplines on dissertation chapters, theses, fellowship applications, Op-Eds, journal articles, and even book manuscripts. I ran yearly workshops for NSF GRFP applications as well as personal statement workshops for the Yale Psychology Department’s Sneak Peek Program.
I’m especially useful if you’re trying to translate technical work for a general audience, how to structure your publication and frame your findings, or need some feedback on a fellowship or grant application.

title: vlad chituc
text:
I’m a postdoctoral researcher at Stanford University, where I work with Michael Frank and Ben Domingue as part of the LEVANTE project. Psychologists often ask people to rate their subjective experience — on a scale from one to ten, how happy are you? how wrong would that be? how strongly are you feeling that emotion? My research draws from sensory psychophysics and information theory to understand what those numbers actually mean.
I completed my PhD in 2024 at Yale University, and my dissertation was advised by Brian Scholl. This work was awarded the Glushko Dissertation Prize from the Cognitive Science Society. [Dissertation] [Glushko Prize Talk @ CogSci 2025]
I’ve written publicly for outlets like The New York Times, The New Republic, and The Daily Beast.
